### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b4624440e699395d1929b1eb7d77f60b4185c481`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b4624440e699395d1929b1eb7d77f60b4185c481` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `62c7615fd7e6b3bcd0b93e649cb3d1ceed6d8164` — the merge of head `c3bf5a3e66c5bda3c3163dba1647a0c68a8245f3` into base `b4624440e699395d1929b1eb7d77f60b4185c481`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 62c7615fd7e6b3bcd0b93e649cb3d1ceed6d8164 && git checkout 62c7615fd7e6b3bcd0b93e649cb3d1ceed6d8164
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b4624440e699395d1929b1eb7d77f60b4185c481 c3bf5a3e66c5bda3c3163dba1647a0c68a8245f3 && git checkout -B drift-repro b4624440e699395d1929b1eb7d77f60b4185c481 && git merge --no-ff c3bf5a3e66c5bda3c3163dba1647a0c68a8245f3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b4624440e699395d1929b1eb7d77f60b4185c481
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b4624440e699395d1929b1eb7d77f60b4185c481` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d7b02edb7d1a385e8c1a2cb0b8265c806d680f29`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.activation-ledger.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/admin-set-switch-off-last-platform-admin.dogfood.test.ts, content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx, .changeset/33082-admin-set-switch-off-last-platform-admin.md + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.re-pricing.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/catalog-activation-door.dogfood.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/catalog-activation-door.test.ts

I read code head `87743b6297cfd180ebc1352f3e54f49ce6027224` and the docs-only delta to this head (`authorization.mdx`).

### ① Derived judgments

- **The verdict is right, and it is wired correctly.** `refuseIfPlatformStandingEnds` reads the `platform-admins` population through the guard's one enumerator, before and after the pending write. `readAdminSetSwitchedOff` simulates the pending ledger row (update, move onto the pair, insert, and the `package_id` holder test), so the "after" read is the guard's own measurement, not a pattern match. Bans are re-read the same way the main verdict does. It runs only for `sys_metadata_activation` and only after the existing early returns: the restore exemption at `before.size === 0`, all-banned, and no addressed rows. So it only adds a refusal, and switching the set on is never refused (after ⊇ before). Under a walled posture the grant half is not counted on either side, so nothing changes there. A configured, verified, unbanned owner keeps "after" non-empty, which is pinned, and `last-admin-guard.re-pricing.test.ts` (config owner plus grant admin → switch-off lands) stays green by construction.
- **must-fix M1: an existing unit pin of the old verdict is not inverted.** `last-admin-guard.test.ts` "an org admin elsewhere keeps the switch-off legal — the invariant is the ENVIRONMENT's" seeds `usr_platform` (grant-anchored) and `usr_owner` (organization owner), then expects `switchOff` to resolve. That is exactly the #33082 shape: the platform population goes {usr_platform} → {}, so this head refuses it and the test turns red. The PR body says this file was not run locally ("needs a built `@objectstack/rest`"). Invert it to a refusal that names the last platform administrator, or fold it into the replacement cases in `.activation-ledger.test.ts` and delete it.
- **must-fix M2: an existing dogfood CONTROL pins the old verdict.** `catalog-activation-door.dogfood.test.ts` "CONTROL: switching `admin_full_access` off with the organization owner still standing lands 200" boots stock `single` with no `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` (its own comment says so) and expects 200. At this head it gets 403, so the dogfood battery the narrowing arm owes is red. Replace it, for example with the refusal plus "no row lands" (the new file already measures the configured-owner pair end to end). Also update the file's header bullet ("landing when one stands") and the comment above the pair ("refuses … only when it would leave nobody who can sign in").
- Docs delta: `authorization.mdx` now states the platform-admin verdict, that a second grant holder does not help, and that a configured owner permits the switch-off. It matches the code. The runtime `catalog-activation-door.test.ts` uses a stubbed write error, so it is unaffected.
- nit N1: `last-admin-guard.test.ts` path-4 header ("where one stands the write is PERMITTED", about a config-anchored administrator) is still true. Once M1 lands, add that an organization owner no longer permits it, so the next reader does not reintroduce the bug.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch`, `fix(plugin-auth)!`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, a BREAKING paragraph naming the affected deployment (stock `single` with no configured owner) and the remedy (`OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL`), and one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker. Correct for a non-protocol narrowing (AGENTS.md). `Metadata-protocol: none` holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Security-relevant (break-glass standing, ADR-0135 D5.2). The change only adds a refusal and never widens, and it is fail-closed through the existing `failClosed` envelope.
- Option B (every standing half) is split to #33423. This PR narrows only the ledger halves, which is the ruled scope.
- CI at `87743b62`: Type Check and Lint were cancelled by the push, not failed. The PR-body guard is red: card #33082 has no `Claim:` naming `claude/area-A2-33082`. That is the area's to fix before landing.

### ④ Design judgment

The bug is a population mismatch: "can sign in" (owners count) was used to answer "can undo this" (only `manage_metadata` holders can). Reading the platform-admin population only for the ledger write, the one write whose undo door needs `manage_metadata`, is the minimal correct fix and matches seat ruling A. Making stock `single` unable to switch the set off without a configured owner is the honest consequence, and the BREAKING text says so. The design holds. The FAIL is about the stale pins only (M1, M2). A test-only plus comment delta that inverts them, with the dogfood battery green at the landing head, converts this to PASS.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c3bf5a3e66c5bda3c3163dba1647a0c68a8245f3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.activation-ledger.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/catalog-activation-door.dogfood.test.ts + packages/qa/dogfood/test/admin-set-switch-off-last-platform-admin.dogfood.test.ts, content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx, .changeset/33082-admin-set-switch-off-last-platform-admin.md

This is the delta `d7b02edb...c3bf5a3e` on my FAIL at `d7b02edb7d1a385e8c1a2cb0b8265c806d680f29`. Everything outside these four files is as I read it there.

### ① Derived judgments

- **M1 closed.** `last-admin-guard.test.ts` "an org admin elsewhere keeps the switch-off legal" is inverted to "#33082 — an org owner elsewhere does NOT keep the switch-off legal": 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, "last platform administrator", and no ledger row.
- **M2 closed.** The dogfood CONTROL is replaced by "the organization owner still standing is refused 403 too, and no row lands", with an anti-vacuity read that the owner really stands. The header bullet and the comment above the pair now state both verdicts.
- **N1 closed.** The path-4 header says an organization owner no longer permits the switch-off.
- **The one code move is an ordering change, and the refusal set is unchanged.** `refuseIfPlatformStandingEnds` now runs only on the branch where the administrators verdict would let the write through (`losing` empty, or survivors left). Where nobody would remain, the main verdict refuses first with its own text. Where that verdict permits, the platform verdict is asked. The set of refused writes is the same union as at `87743b62`; only which message wins for an all-empty write changes, so every existing refusal keeps its text. The ledger-only scope, the restore exemption and the early returns are untouched. The new unit pin (second grant holder plus owner → the platform message names both holders) measures the platform branch where the administrators verdict permits.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from my record at `d7b02edb`: `@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch`, `fix(plugin-auth)!`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, BREAKING, one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Security-relevant (break-glass standing). The change only adds a refusal and stays fail-closed.
- CI at this head was still running when I read it. The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head, and the full dogfood battery owed by the narrowing arm (including `catalog-activation-door` and the new `admin-set-switch-off-last-platform-admin`) must be green there. The PR-body claim guard must also be green there.

### ④ Design judgment

Unchanged: this fixes the population mismatch ("can sign in" used for "can undo"), scoped to the ledger write, per seat ruling A. Asking the platform verdict only after the main verdict permits is cleaner than the first head, because each verdict owns its own message.

Implemented-by: `claude/area-A2-33082`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4d1PGptBW3QRQNmy5e6`

**VERDICT: PASS**
